title: Inertia: the coin and the card (জড়তা: কয়েন ও কার্ড)
placement: Book pages 64–65, topic 3.1.1: জড়তা (Inertia). Next to the definition of জড়তা and স্থিতি জড়তা, as a home experiment for inertia of rest.
description: Interactive 3D figure for inertia of rest (স্থিতি জড়তা), book pages 64–65, topic 3.1.1: the classic coin-and-card trick. A card lies on a glass on a small sand-coloured tabletop in a calm deep-blue setting, with a ৫ টাকা coin on it; the student taps the card and a finger flicks it hard (shown 10x slower, said in the panel). The card shoots away at 2.2 m/s; friction (μ = 0.25) acts on the coin only while the card slides under it (a few hundredths of a second), so the coin gets only a few cm/s, stays where it was and drops straight into the glass. A white-rimmed blue arrow on the card and an orange one on the coin show each one's speed along the table; the panel gives both speeds in m/s and the book's explanation; labels say what each does while it is true. Test tab: 3 questions (what the coin does, which inertia it is and why, which one moves fast just after the flick); after each answer the scene plays on and shows it. Phone-first, Bangla.
